question: Environmental impact assessment for the A16 Motorway Bari-Mola di Bari bypass project

The Apulia Region’s Landscape Monitoring and Planning Office has issued an unfavourable opinion as part of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) procedure for the proposed construction of a bypass between Bari and Mola di Bari on the A 16 Motorway, arguing that the project would not conform with its landscape plan.

The office argued that ‘in the interests of landscape protection, upgrading existing infrastructures is preferable to building new ones so long as such an approach is shown to be technically and financially feasible. The studies carried out by the developer (ANAS) do not demonstrate that Alternative 3 is the least impactful of the technically feasible proposals.

Widening Highway 16 (Alternative 1) would lead to less direct and indirect land take and cause less territorial fragmentation than Alternative 3.’ The Landscape Monitoring and Planning Office added that ‘the choice of Alternative 3 cannot be justified on the grounds of landscape and environmental compatibility’1. In the light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission make its evaluation of Italy’s second flood risk management plan public?
Has Italy set targets to reduce net land take by 2030?
Does the Commission believe that the alternative that has the least impact on the landscape should be chosen for this project?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.3.2024) 1. The Commission is in the process of evaluating the Member States’ second flood risk management plans, including Italy’s, and plans to make the results of its evaluations publicly available in the course of 2024. 2. The EU Soil Strategy for 20301 called Member States to voluntarily set national land take reduction targets by 2023.

This action will be followed up in due course. The Commission proposal on the Soil Monitoring Law2 – currently in co-decision – also provides for mitigation principles that the Member States must follow in the event of land take. At this stage, the Commission has no information as to whether any target on land take has been set by Italy. 3.

In accordance with Article 5(1)(d) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive3, a developer is required to describe in the environmental impact assessment report the studied reasonable alternatives (in terms of project design, technology, location, size and scale) relevant to the project and its specific characteristics as well as the main reasons for the option chosen, taking into account the effects of the project on the environmental factors (including on the landscape) under Article 3.
1 Commission Communication ‘EU Soil Strategy for 2030 - Reaping the benefits of healthy soils for people,

food, nature and climate’ (COM(2021) 699 final). 2 Proposal for a Directive on Soil Monitoring and Resilience (COM(2023) 416 final). 3 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1–21, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014, p. 1–18.
